purpose: Paste-ready issue body amendments for the user-approved aid-evidence direction. Preserve original issue scope and required human evidence while removing obsolete budgeting/server-plaintext assumptions. No GitHub writes were made.

issues.title: Write and approve the Scryer v1 product contract
issues.body:
Description: Document Scryer as a student-aid evidence reconciliation app: primary user, mission, supported aid/school/refund/bank evidence, exact supported claims, synthetic demo and self-host behavior, non-goals and the complete review → correction → source-linked explanation → encrypted save/recovery → optional sync → export/delete journey. Replace the earlier budget stage with supported aid reconciliation; do not imply budgets, net worth or entitlement. Keep December 31, 2026 public self-service signup with real records and $0 required cash hosting as the observable release target, with explicit blocking gates.

Done when: the contract is checked into README.md with current-versus-target capabilities, measurable completion, supported data/non-goals and the complete journey, and maintainers approve the amended contract through normal review. Writing this contract does not require or certify the later public deployment.

Depends on: #32.

issues.title: Map the user journeys and failure states
issues.body:
Description: Specify first-run/local-versus-sync accounts, unlock/recovery, supported/unsupported import, column/money mapping, duplicates, review/approval, corrections, source-linked insights, unknown coverage, offline/stale/conflicting sync, encrypted export/restore and separate local-case/synced-case/account deletion. Include empty, waiting, error, retry and safe-exit states. The aid-evidence insight replaces the former budget/dashboard stage.

Done when: README.md links a complete reachable screenflow graph and navigable low-fidelity prototype; risky actions explain exact scope and require fresh review; two actual consenting people outside implementation test the design and observations, design fixes and necessary retests are recorded before further full personal-case UI implementation. Automation cannot replace these sessions. Existing component development is not retroactively claimed to follow the study.

Depends on: #33, #36, #37.

issues.title: Record the architecture and service boundaries
issues.body:
Description: Record Next.js owning the user interface, bounded browser import workers producing unreviewed proposals, a C++20 exact semantic core with independent Python oracle, browser-owned plaintext/encryption/local storage, FastAPI authenticating and persisting opaque ciphertext, and PostgreSQL providing durable tenant-isolated storage. Define typed boundaries and local/target deployment and dataflow diagrams. Replace server-side plaintext financial rules and the proposed SQLAlchemy/Alembic authority with browser semantic validation and one checksum-verified SQL migration runner using explicit psycopg transactions. Document how inactive Prisma scaffolding will be inventoried and retired safely.

Done when: README.md contains the diagrams, component responsibilities, invariants, rejected alternatives, migration authority and step-by-step Prisma retirement plan; maintainers adopt the intentional financial-rule/migration changes. Next.js UI is retained; no NextUI component-library requirement is asserted. Physical legacy cleanup, WASM integration, hosted operation and complete product implementation remain separately tracked work.

Depends on: #32, #33, #36, #37.

issues.title: Specify financial invariants and formulas
issues.body:
Description: Specify exact signed integer-cent transport, nonnegative approved fact magnitudes and role-derived signs, checked arithmetic, dates/observation/review knowledge, correction/branch rules, source/recipient provenance and visible unknown coverage. Define school-credit-minus-school-charge surplus, exact change attribution and separate aid lifecycle/refund/bank-match observations. Explicitly reject unsupported income/expense budgets, categories, transfer classification, opening balances and net-worth inference.

Done when: README.md and hand-calculated executable examples agree for normal purchases, school/merchant refunds, both imported transfer accounts, missing income evidence, partial months and conflicting corrections; Python and native C++ agree; incomplete history never becomes a complete balance/net-worth or entitlement claim. Maintainers adopt these aid-specific formulas in place of the obsolete budgeting formulas. Browser/WASM release parity is separately tracked.

Depends on: #33.
